title: Domains in henselian parameter-root towers and their filtered colimits
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], with $C$ a Noetherian ring and $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, $r\geq0$. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$ is nonempty connected and that at every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C$ the tuple $(t_i)$ is a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in $C_{\mathfrak m}$ with regular local quotient [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For each $n>0$ set $K_n=C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)$ using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $K_n$ is finite free over $C$ with basis $x^a$, $0\leq a_i<n$, is regular Noetherian, and is a nonzero domain. Every maximal ideal of $K_n$ contains all $x_i$; in its local ring the $x_i$ are a regular sequence and the quotient is $C_{\mathfrak m}/J C_{\mathfrak m}$, where $\mathfrak m$ is its contraction. The ring $C=K_1$ is a nonzero domain, and $f=\prod_i t_i$ is nonzero in every $K_n$. More generally let $(C_\lambda,J_\lambda)$ be a small nonempty filtered diagram of such pairs with the same $r$, unital transition maps carrying each labelled $t_i$ to the next one, and $J_\lambda=(t_i)$. Put $H=\varinjlim_\lambda C_\lambda$, $H_n=H[x_i]/(x_i^n-t_i)$, and $H_\infty=\varinjlim_n H_n$, with power maps for divisibility, over all positive $n$ or only those prime to a fixed positive prime. Then $H_n=\varinjlim_\lambda K_{\lambda,n}$ and $H$, every $H_n$, and $H_\infty$ are nonzero domains in which $f\ne0$. The spectra of these rings and of their localizations at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] are nonempty connected qcqs. For $r=0$, $f=1$ and the root algebras are the base rings. For any henselian regular Noetherian local ring $R$ and any partial regular system of parameters, its finite and full root rings and their punctures have the same nonzero-domain and nonempty-connected conclusions, without requiring the parameter ideal to be the maximal ideal.

proof.text:
First $J$ lies in every maximal ideal of $C$. Indeed, if $J+\mathfrak m=C$, the finite $C$-algebra $C/(J\cap\mathfrak m)\simeq C/J	imes C/\mathfrak m$ has an idempotent $(0,1)
e0$ which reduces to zero modulo $J$, contradicting uniqueness in the henselian-pair definition. Here the displayed isomorphism sends $c$ to its two residues; surjectivity follows by writing $1=j+u$ with $j\in J,u\in\mathfrak m$. Nonemptiness of $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$ gives $C/J
e0$ and $C
e0$.

proof.text: Use the proved simultaneous-root algebra API: its bounded-monomial basis gives finite freeness, faithful flatness and an injective coefficient map. Finite algebras over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian.

The finite algebra $K_n$ is integral over $C$. If $\mathfrak q$ is a maximal ideal of $K_n$, its contraction $\mathfrak m$ is maximal in $C$, and $JK_n\subset\mathfrak q$ because $J$ lies in the Jacobson radical. As $x_i^n=t_i\in\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q$ is prime, each $x_i\in\mathfrak q$. Eliminating all root variables gives $K_n/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\simeq C/J$. Localization of this quotient at $\mathfrak q$ identifies $(K_n)_{\mathfrak q}/(x_i)$ with $C_{\mathfrak m}/JC_{\mathfrak m}$: the corresponding prime of $C/J$ is $\mathfrak m/J$, since all roots vanish.

The finite free coefficient map is flat, hence its local map C_m to (K_n)_q is flat. The assumed regular sequence t_i becomes weakly regular after this flat base change. Its entries are x_i^n. They lie in the maximal ideal, so weak regularity is regularity. The positive-power regular-sequence equivalence reflects this to regularity of the x_i. This also works for n=1 and the empty sequence.

source.place: Tags 04GG (monic quotient basis), 00CS (proposition-localization-exact), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); explicit companion-coordinate calculation for the simultaneous root presentation of ILO IX Proposition 2.1.

proof.text: The local ring $(K_n)_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian by localization. Apply the regular-sequence lifting criterion to the sequence and quotient of Steps 3 and 4 to conclude it is regular local. Every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $K_n$ is contained in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$, and $(K_n)_{\mathfrak p}$ is the localization of $(K_n)_{\mathfrak q}$ at the corresponding prime (both rings invert exactly the required denominators). The localization theorem for regular local rings therefore proves regularity at every prime. This proves that $K_n$ is a regular Noetherian ring.

Let L=(x_i) and I=JK_n. Since x_i^n=t_i, L is contained in the radical of I. If two idempotents have the same image modulo L, their images modulo I differ by a nilpotent, and are equal by uniqueness of idempotents modulo a nil ideal. Uniqueness of henselian integral idempotent lifting then makes the original idempotents equal. The explicit equivalence K_n/L ≃ C/J and connectedness of Spec(C/J) now show every idempotent of K_n is zero or one. Since K_n is nonzero, its spectrum is connected.

The spectrum of $K_n$ is regular: affine stalks are the prime localizations proved regular in Step 5. A nonempty connected regular scheme is integral. By the definition of an integral scheme, its ring of global sections $K_n$ is a nonzero domain. For $n=1$, elimination of $x_i=t_i$ identifies $K_1$ with $C$, so $C$ is also a nonzero domain. Each $t_j$ is nonzero in $C$: in any maximal localization its image acts injectively on the nonzero quotient $C_{\mathfrak m}/(t_1,\ldots,t_{j-1})$, so that image cannot be zero. Thus $f=\prod_i t_i\ne0$ in $C$, and it stays nonzero in every $K_n$ by the injective coefficient map of Step 2.

Apply the existing filtered-colimit domain theorem to the coefficient diagram. For the labelled product, eventual equality with zero in the colimit would give equality with zero at a common later stage. Compatibility of the labelled parameters carries the product to that later product, which is nonzero by the finite-pair result.

proof.text: For fixed $n$, the coefficient maps and labelled roots give a cocone $K_{\lambda,n}\to H_n$. It is colimiting: a compatible family $K_{\lambda,n}\to A$ restricts to a unique map $H\to A$, and the images of each labelled root are independent of stage by filteredness; they satisfy $x_i^n=t_i$. The polynomial-quotient presentation therefore gives a unique map $H_n\to A$, inverse to restriction on cocones. This proves the canonical identification $H_n\simeq\varinjlim_\lambda K_{\lambda,n}$. The same common-stage argument of Step 8 makes $H_n$ a nonzero domain and keeps $f$ nonzero, since every later $K_{\lambda,n}$ has these properties by Step 7.

proof.text: Use the proved compatible-root quotient colimit API. Its directed index wrapper orders positive allowed orders by divisibility, and its transition, inclusion and universal-property lemmas construct the colimit cocone with vertex tameRootAlgebra. Apply the filtered-colimit domain theorem and the same common-stage argument to the coefficient product. No injectivity of transitions is required.

proof.text:
For each domain $A$ obtained above with $f
e0$, the localization $A[1/f]$ is a nonzero domain: fractions multiply as usual; a fraction is zero exactly when $f^k a=0$ for some $k$, which in a domain forces $a=0$. For any nonzero domain $B$, its zero ideal is prime and is a point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ contained in every nonempty basic open $D(b)$, because $D(b)
e\varnothing$ implies $b
e0$. Thus this point is dense and the spectrum is nonempty irreducible, hence connected. Finally every displayed spectrum, including these localizations, is affine and therefore qcqs. These arguments apply to $C,K_n,H,H_n,H_\infty$ and all their punctures, irrespective of Noetherianity at the colimit.

proof.text:
For the final local-ring clause, let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian regular Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$, and let the chosen partial parameter list be $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, $0\leq r\leq d$, the first $r$ entries (after reordering) of a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. For each $n>0$, [lem-sfb-henselian-parameter-root-regularity] applied to $R$, $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, $r$ and $n$ says that $K_n=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)$ is free over $R$ on the bounded monomials, so $R	o K_n$ is injective, and that $K_n$ is a henselian regular local domain. That node uses only the maximal-ideal pair $(R,\mathfrak m)$; it does not need the partial parameter ideal $(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ to be henselian or maximal, and it does not need $n$ to be invertible. For $n=1$, $K_1=R$, so $R$ is a nonzero domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ is a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. As in Step 7, each $t_j$ therefore acts injectively on the nonzero ring $R/(t_1,\ldots,t_{j-1})$ and is nonzero. Hence $f=\prod_i t_i
eq0$ in the domain $R$, and $f
eq0$ in every $K_n$ because $R	o K_n$ is injective. Now take the constant one-object diagram with value $R$. It is nonempty and filtered, and for it $H=R$ and $H_n=K_n$. Since every $K_n$ is a nonzero domain with $f
eq0$, the representative and common-stage argument of Step 10 applies, again using [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], to the divisibility diagram of the $K_n$, over all positive $n$ or only those prime to a fixed prime. So the full root ring $\varinjlim_nK_n$ is a nonzero domain with $f
eq0$. Step 11 then shows that $K_n[1/f]$ and $(\varinjlim_nK_n)[1/f]$ are nonzero domains, and that all these spectra are nonempty, connected and qcqs. If $r=0$, every root algebra is $R$ by its presentation and $f=1$.
